candidate.answerReason: Every solution has odd \(y\), and positivity restricts \(y\) to \(1,3,\ldots,253\). Each of these 127 values gives exactly one positive integer \(x\).

methods.label: Use parity and positivity
methods.explanation:
Because \(2x\) is even and \(763\) is odd, \(3y\) must be odd. Thus \(y\) is odd.

The condition \(x\ge1\) gives
\[
3y=763-2x\le761,
\]
so the positive integer \(y\) is at most \(253\). Its possible values are therefore
\[
1,3,5,\ldots,253.
\]
For every value in this list,
\[
x=\frac{763-3y}{2}
\]
is an integer because the numerator is even, and it is at least \((763-3\cdot253)/2=2\). Thus every listed value works. Each determines one \(x\), so no solution is omitted or counted twice.

There are
\[
\frac{253-1}{2}+1=127
\]
values in the list. The answer is \(\boxed{127}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Parity, a simple inequality, and counting an equally spaced list provide a complete elementary solution.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is finding and counting all solutions under integer and positivity restrictions. Parity determines which values can be integral, and a linear bound makes the search finite. The one-to-one correspondence between eligible values of y and solution pairs establishes completeness.

review.mathematicalCheck: Necessity restricts y to the odd integers from 1 through 253. Each gives exactly one positive integer x, so the count is 127.
